newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Banks lead Caracas stock exchange higher.
newsitem.headline: Banks lead Caracas stock exchange higher.

text.p: Financial stocks, buoyed by news of that a Spanish bank is seeking a large stake in the country's leading bank, led the Caracas Stock Exchange higher in strong trading Thursday, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index rose 1.03 percent to 6,195.48 as 22 stocks rose, 12 slipped and 10 closed flat.
Brokers said news that Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya was in talks with France's Credit Lyonnais to buy its 17 percent in top Venezuelan bank Banco Provincial had a positive impact on the market.
Banco Provincial rose 52.25 bolivars to 1222.25 bolivars and Banco Mercantil, the country's second largest bank, rose 80.00 bolivars to 1500.00 bolivars.
The sale of state-owned Banco Consolidado and Banco de Venezuela later this month had also stimulated the market, brokers said.

Among non-financial stocks, recently-debuted national telephone company CANTV led the way, climbing 81.00 bolivars to 1880.00 bolivars. Utility Electricidad de Caracas meanwhile slipped 3.00 bolivars to 518.00 bolivars.
Total trade was 4.940 billion bolivars ($10.5 million).
